chunks: What Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Sulaymān ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام, who said:
"When you wish to perform ghusl for Friday, then perform wudu (ablution) and perform ghusl."

The strongest indication for that is that wudu (ablution) is an obligation, and it is not permissible to render salat (prayer) permissible without it except by a legal proof. And there is no legal proof here for the dropping of ritual purity for these ghusls that would remove excuse; so it is necessary that its obligation remain binding. And the like of that does not bind us regarding its dropping in ghusl of janabah, because we only said that on the basis of proof, namely the consensus of the sect that when ghusl of janabah and purification from wudu (ablution) come together, the ghusl suffices for both of them; and what we have narrated from the hadiths confirms that and increases it in clarification.

key_terms.إِجْمَاعُ الْعِصَابَةِ: the consensus of the Imamiyyah scholars and transmitters
key_terms.الطَّهَارَةِ: ritual purity required for validity of worship such as salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْأَحَادِيثِ: the transmitted hadith reports used as supporting evidence
key_terms.الْأَغْسَالِ: ritual baths other than the specific case under discussion
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing ordinarily required before salat (prayer)
key_terms.دَلِيلٍ شَرْعِيٍّ: a legal proof from the Sacred Law establishing or negating a ruling
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ghusl performed for the state of janabah
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ: an obligatory duty established in the Sacred Law

ai.seo_question: Does Friday ghusl remove the need for wudu (ablution), or must wudu still be performed before salat?
ai.summary: This report states that for the ghusl of Friday, one should perform wudu (ablution) and then ghusl. The accompanying legal discussion argues that wudu (ablution) remains obligatory for such ghusls unless there is a specific shar'i proof removing it, while ghusl of janabah is treated differently because of established proof and the consensus of the Imamiyyah that it suffices in place of wudu (ablution).
